---
title: "Presampling for sources that read the oracle independently"
subtitle: "Does a random oracle decompose into bit-fixing mixtures when the advice is produced by parties who never communicate?"
---

Presampling is the standard route to non-uniform security in idealized models. A random oracle together with $S$ bits of oracle-dependent advice is close to a mixture of oracles fixed on $P$ points and uniform elsewhere, at a cost of roughly $ST/P$ against $T$-query adversaries. The technique assumes **one** preprocessing stage, and it is not known how to run it when the advice comes from several parties who read the oracle independently.

That is the setting of multi-source randomness extraction in the random-oracle model, and the reason to want a decomposition route is concrete: the compression argument that gets the bounds instead stalls for non-monolithic constructions such as Merkle-Damgård and sponge.

## The lattice

Two statements live in this setting, and they are not the same statement. The page under this hub carries the **parallel form** since 1 September 2026; the **mixture form** is what it carried before, and is what the campaign attacks.

| | Parallel form | Mixture form |
|---|---|---|
| What is asked | each stage marks its own list, from the whole oracle but only its own leakage and coins | one joint mixture, chosen with every leakage in hand but forbidden the points |
| Who the adversary is | the online distinguisher, reading all the advice | a challenge-oblivious observer, reading the leakage and $H(\mathbf{x})$ but not $\mathbf{x}$ |
| $\ell = 2$, $q = 0$ | **Open.** | Proved, and tight. |
| $\ell = 2$, $q = 1$ | **Open.** | Proved, under an extra hypothesis. |
| $\ell = 2$, $q \geq 2$ | **Open.** | **Open.** |
| $\ell \geq 3$, any $q$ | **Open.** | **Open.** |

Neither form is known to imply the other. They differ in three places at once: the mixture is joint where the selectors are split; but it is forbidden the points, where each selector may read its own; and its observer is challenge-oblivious by fiat, where in the parallel form that restriction belongs to the application and the conjecture's own distinguisher reads everything. Nothing is proved of the parallel form. Everything proved in the right-hand column is a two-source argument that has not been re-derived for $\ell \geq 3$.

A separate question lives on the $\ell$ axis and is easy to miss: both conjectured errors carry $\sqrt{\delta}$ at every $\ell$, while the compression bound of Coretti, Farshim, Harasser and Southern improves as $\delta^{\ell/2}$, each additional source making the challenge harder to hit. Whether a decomposition bound admits the same improvement is open, and is not the same question as $q \geq 2$.

Two features of the setting are load-bearing rather than incidental, and a proposed proof that does not use them is wrong.

- **More than one source.** Extraction is *false* at $\ell = 1$, and the counterexample is explicit: a source that queries $H$ at its own output point and leaks one bit of the answer defeats every admissible family. So a proof cannot draw its use of independence solely from a bound on the probability that the fixed set contains the challenge, because such bounds hold for one source too.

## Why it is worth stating separately

A decomposition would give extraction bounds for split unpredictable sources as a corollary, of the shape $\kappa(q) = O(\sqrt{\sigma' q^{+} \delta})$, without going through compression. The conditional theorems are proved --- for the parallel form, by way of a transfer to the ordinary bit-fixing model that carries every bound already proved there --- and what is missing in both cases is the hypothesis. The extraction bound itself is known unconditionally by compression, with an incomparable constant and domain dependence; what a decomposition would add is the route, and the route is what reaches the non-monolithic constructions that compression cannot.

## Sources

- Coretti, Farshim, Harasser, and Southern. [*Multi-Source Randomness Extraction and Generation in the Random-Oracle Model*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1258). ITC 2025. The paper that raises the decomposition question and obtains its bounds by compression instead.
- Coretti, Dodis, Guo, and Steinberger. [*Random Oracles and Non-Uniformity*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/937). EUROCRYPT 2018, pages 227–258.
- Dodis, Guo, and Katz. [*Fixing Cracks in the Concrete: Random Oracles with Auxiliary Input, Revisited*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-56614-6_16). EUROCRYPT 2017, pages 473–495.
- Unruh. *Random Oracles and Auxiliary Input*. CRYPTO 2007, pages 205–223.
